resolution_note: Decided by Hassan Jalal, 2026-10-06. created_at is the device clock at draft creation, in UTC; a draft whose Submit was pressed follows DG-65 instead. Confirmed by Hassan Jalal, 2026-10-07: 48 hours at most, unless an explicitly approved requirement says otherwise

title: Submission only on the reporter's explicit Submit; 48-hour retries; status check before a retry or deletion
source_refs: Mobile SRS v2.2.0 FR-PUB.28, FR-PUB.29, FR-COMMON.12, §3.6.4; DG-14; DG-55
recommendation: A draft is never submitted automatically: submission starts only when the reporter presses Submit after reviewing the report. A failed submission is then retried for up to 48 hours from the first submission attempt, with the same identifier and idempotency key. Retries stop on confirmed success or cancellation, and no duplicate report is ever created. An unsubmitted draft is told apart from a submission whose response was lost: before retrying or deleting local data, the client checks the submission's status on the server. A draft whose Submit was never pressed stays a temporary draft and is deleted at the end of its 2-day lifetime
resolution_note: Decided by Hassan Jalal, 2026-10-06. Refines DG-14. A submission still unconfirmed when its 48 hours end is DG-67. 2026-10-07 (DG-67): at the end of the 48 hours the local copy is deleted even when the server cannot be reached for the status check; the server keeps any report that exists

title: Does amending SC-10 lapse the DR-26 override?
source_refs: Mobile SRS v2.2.0 §1.4.3.2 (DR-26 condition), §7.4.2 SC-10; DG-63
recommendation: Treat it as an amendment by the authority that set the condition, not a descoping: SC-10 stays in force as amended (operating-system protections, account binding, the 2-day lifetime and no backups for drafts and media; tokens in secure storage), so the override stands. Confirm
resolution_note: Decided by Hassan Jalal, 2026-10-07, after reviewing docs/planning/DR-26_REVIEW.md: DR-26 remains active and is not cancelled. It governs the architecture (the citizen, staff, Union Council, contractor and Mayor & Operations portals within the approved React Native application) and is not fundamentally a draft-encryption decision. The SC-10 amendment of 2026-10-06 (DG-63) is an explicit owner-approved amendment of the controls associated with DR-26, not a failure of its condition and not grounds for it to lapse. Scope: citizen-side drafts and pending submissions need no Parakh-specific encryption key, draft lock or application-encrypted draft store beyond the operating system's protections, the app sandbox and the approved backup exclusion (DG-59). It weakens no unrelated control and is not extended to future staff, Union Council, contractor, Mayor or administrative data (DG-68). Mobile SRS v2.5.0: TBD-M16 resolved. No implementation change was needed

title: A submission still unconfirmed when its 48-hour retry window ends
source_refs: DG-14; DG-64; DG-65; Mobile SRS v2.3.0 TBD-M15
recommendation: Keep it, labelled not confirmed, until a server check settles it: if the report exists, show its reference and delete the local copy; if not, keep it for the reporter's retry or cancellation for at most 2 more days (4 days after the first submission attempt), then delete it with a plain notice
resolution_note: Decided by Hassan Jalal, 2026-10-07, differently from the proposal: a pending submission is retried for up to 48 hours from the original submission attempt (the first press of Submit) and, if still not confirmed, is deleted from the phone; failed or unconfirmed submissions are never kept beyond that. While pending it is shown apart from saved drafts and marked not yet confirmed. Implemented 2026-10-07: submission_expires_at = submission_requested_at + 48 hours, fixed at the first press; a last status check where the server can be reached, then deletion with a request to the server to drop its temporary copy (the server keeps any report that exists). Supersedes DG-14's 'keep the local draft' clause and amends DG-65's status check before deletion. Mobile SRS v2.4.0: TBD-M15 resolved

title: CIT-08: capture settings — photo size and quality, and the video bitrate (NFR-8 and DG-54 set no number)
source_refs: Mobile SRS v2.5.0 NFR-8 (as amended at v2.3.0), FR-PUB.4, FR-COMMON.14; DG-54 (720p, 60 s, 40 MiB); docs/api/CITIZEN_REPORTING_CONTRACT.md (photo 10 MiB, video 40 MiB); T-049 phone test, finding F-2
current_authority: NFR-8: keep images small through the camera's quality and picture-size settings, with no second copy; no value is set. DG-54: 720p, at most 60 seconds and 40 MiB, encoding settings routine and reversible; no bitrate is set
recommendation: PROPOSED technical defaults (mobile/src/domain/captureSettings.ts): photos at the largest picture size at or below about 3.2 megapixels and JPEG quality 0.7 (on the test phone: 2.76 MP, about 0.2 MB); video at 4.5 Mbit/s, so 60 seconds with sound fits the 40 MiB limit (at the phone's default 12 Mbit/s a recording stopped after 26 seconds, F-2); a capture starts only with 25 MiB free for a photo or 65 MiB for a video.
